title: METR Measurement Workflow
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI-Native Schools
description: Read the six steps that turn AI task results into a 50 percent time horizon, then answer five questions about the steps.

educational.topic: How a 50 percent time horizon is measured
learningObjectives: The learner will explain the six steps that turn AI task results into a 50 percent time horizon, correctly answering at least four of five questions about the steps.
prerequisites: Benchmark task suite, human working time, task success rate, task horizon, and 50 percent time horizon, from the section "METR and the Task-Horizon Idea" in Chapter 4.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore a process diagram, then answer questions that use the order and the unit of measure
keyQuestions: Where does the 50 percent horizon come from?
commonMisconceptions: The horizon measures how long the AI takes to run
A 50 percent horizon means the AI is reliable on tasks up to that length
The task suite is a single test with one score
assessmentOpportunities: What unit measures how long a task is?
A model has a 50 percent horizon of 2 hours. What does that mean?
A model succeeds on 9 of 10 attempts. What is the task success rate?
Why is human time used instead of AI running time?

controls.name: Steps in the flowchart
controls.description: click (or tab to and press Enter) to read a step's description. The step turns gold; steps you have read turn green.

controls.name: Answer options and Submit
controls.description: choose one option and press Submit. One attempt per question; the correct option is then shown.

controls.name: Next and Try again
controls.description: move through the questions, and restart them after the score.
